questions.q: Where does Msimangu arrange for Kumalo to sleep?
choices: In the house of Mrs Lithebe, a good church member who is an Msutu but speaks Zulu well
In a boarding house in Claremont
questions.explain: The room costs three shillings a week and meals can be taken with the people of the Mission.

questions.q: What does Kumalo tell the priests at dinner about his home district?
choices: That it is prosperous and growing
About the sickness of the land — vanished grass, dongas, a land of old people and children, the broken tribe
That he wants to leave it for the city
questions.explain: He speaks of the eroded, failing land 'and the love of them must have been in his voice' — but says nothing of Gertrude or Absalom.

questions.q: What newspaper headline is shown to Kumalo at dinner?
choices: A gold strike in the Free State
An old couple robbed and beaten in a lonely house, four natives arrested
questions.explain: A priest shows him the Johannesburg paper in 'bold black letters' — the kind of crime headline white Johannesburg dreads.

questions.q: How does Msimangu describe Gertrude's sickness?
choices: Not that kind of sickness — 'another, a worse kind'; it would be truer to say 'she has many husbands'
questions.explain: Gertrude makes and sells strong illicit liquor, sells herself, has been in prison more than once, and lives in Claremont, one of the worst places in Johannesburg.

questions.q: What does Msimangu say has become of Kumalo's brother John?
choices: He has become one of their great politicians and has no use for the Church any more
questions.explain: John says 'that what God has not done for South Africa, man must do.'

questions.q: Which line of Msimangu's captures his view of the country's crisis?
choices: 'The land will heal itself in time.'
'The tragedy is not that things are broken. The tragedy is that they are not mended again.'
questions.explain: He adds that the white man broke the tribe but has not built anything in its place: 'It is fear that rules this land.'

questions.q: Whom does Msimangu suggest Kumalo talk to about these hard matters — 'a white man and can say what must be said'?
choices: Father Vincent, the priest 'with the boy's cheeks'
questions.explain: Father Vincent is the rosy-cheeked young priest from England who wanted to hear more about Kumalo's country.

questions.q: Why was Msimangu 'firstly' asked to send for Kumalo about Gertrude?
choices: Because she owed the church money
Because she is a woman that is alone, and secondly because her brother is a priest
Because she had asked for him by name
questions.explain: Msimangu also hopes that if Kumalo cannot save the mother, he can at least save her child.

questions.q: When Kumalo calls him kind, how does Msimangu answer?
choices: 'I am not kind. I am a selfish and sinful man, but God put his hands on me, that is all.'
'The Church pays me to be kind.'
questions.explain: He repeats this self-description more than once through the novel.

questions.q: What single word closes the chapter as Kumalo lies in the small clean room?
questions.explain: 'Who could believe it?' — the vast, roaring city named twice.
